title: Heterojunction Band Alignment Visualizer
description: Two semiconductors chosen from menus are drawn on a common vacuum level with their electron affinities, bandgaps, and Fermi levels. The sim computes the conduction and valence band offsets with Anderson's rule, classifies the junction as Type I, Type II, or Type III, states where electrons and holes collect, and sketches the junction in equilibrium. A slider sets the aluminum fraction of AlGaAs.

educational.topic: Band alignment and band offsets at semiconductor heterojunctions
learningObjectives: Identify Type I, Type II, and Type III alignment from a band diagram
Calculate the band offsets of a heterojunction with Anderson's rule
Predict where electrons and holes are confined for a given pair of materials
prerequisites: Energy band diagrams and the Fermi level

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Material menus and an alloy slider with two linked band diagrams and a worked-calculation panel
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Predict-test-observe: students predict the alignment type and the carrier locations, then check the classification and the arithmetic
assessmentOpportunities: Compute both band offsets by hand from the displayed electron affinities and bandgaps
Find one material pair of each alignment type
Explain why the doping type does not change the offsets

assumptions: 300 K bandgaps and commonly tabulated electron affinities
AlGaAs uses the measured 67:33 offset split of Section 12.6.1 through an effective electron affinity
Fermi level placed 0.10 eV from the majority band edge; equilibrium band bending split equally between the two sides
limitations: Anderson's rule ignores interface dipoles and strain; measured offsets can differ by a few tenths of an eV
Lattice mismatch between the chosen materials is ignored
AlN and ZnO from the chapter specification are left out because their published electron affinities disagree too much
